statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-119170 is a regression in Python 3.14.10 in how the hashlib module enforces the algorithms OpenSSL allows in FIPS mode; it affects only a Python whose OpenSSL runs in FIPS mode. OpenSSL in the DockVault image cannot run in FIPS mode: the image ships no FIPS provider (/usr/lib/ossl-modules holds only legacy.so), its /etc/ssl/openssl.cnf enables none, neither the image nor its Compose files set OPENSSL_CONF or OPENSSL_MODULES, and nothing in the application enables FIPS mode, so _hashlib.get_fips_mode() returns 0 and the code with the flaw never runs. The statement is bound to Python 3.14.10 and ends when the base image moves to a Python release without the flaw. Verified for source revision __SOURCE_REVISION__.

CVE-2026-88822 is a flaw in OpenSSL's QUIC implementation, rated Low by OpenSSL: automated peer detection on an already connected socket reads the peer address into a buffer too small for IPv6, so uninitialised stack bytes become the destination of outgoing QUIC packets. It is reached only by an application that runs a QUIC connection with OpenSSL. In this image the system OpenSSL, Alpine's libssl3 and libcrypto3 3.5.9-r0, is used by Python's _ssl module (TLS over TCP), Python's _hashlib module (digests, HMAC, PBKDF2 and scrypt, no ciphers), busybox's ssl_client and apk-tools (TLS over TCP), and the legacy provider and engines OpenSSL loads on request. None of them imports a QUIC or CMS function or names the AES-GCM-SIV cipher, and the image has no openssl command. Python's ssl module has no QUIC support, and dnspython's DNS over QUIC needs aioquic, which the image does not install. The statement is bound to libssl3 and libcrypto3 3.5.9-r0 and ends when the image moves to an OpenSSL with the fix (3.5.10, or Alpine's patched 3.5.9-r1). Verified for source revision __SOURCE_REVISION__.

CVE-2026-88823 is a flaw in OpenSSL's AES-GCM-SIV cipher, rated Low by OpenSSL: an empty additional-data update discards the additional data given before it, and setting a new key or nonce keeps the old additional data. It is reached only by an application that encrypts or decrypts with AES-GCM-SIV through OpenSSL. In this image the system OpenSSL, Alpine's libssl3 and libcrypto3 3.5.9-r0, is used by Python's _ssl module (TLS over TCP), Python's _hashlib module (digests, HMAC, PBKDF2 and scrypt, no ciphers), busybox's ssl_client and apk-tools (TLS over TCP), and the legacy provider and engines OpenSSL loads on request. None of them imports a QUIC or CMS function or names the AES-GCM-SIV cipher, and the image has no openssl command. TLS has no AES-GCM-SIV cipher suite, and the application's own encryption uses AES-GCM through the cryptography package, which carries its own OpenSSL; no code in the image uses AES-GCM-SIV. The statement is bound to libssl3 and libcrypto3 3.5.9-r0 and ends when the image moves to an OpenSSL with the fix (3.5.10, or Alpine's patched 3.5.9-r1). Verified for source revision __SOURCE_REVISION__.

It is reached only by an application that opens a QUIC connection with OpenSSL. In this image the system OpenSSL, Alpine's libssl3 and libcrypto3 3.5.9-r0, is used by Python's _ssl module (TLS over TCP), Python's _hashlib module (digests, HMAC, PBKDF2 and scrypt, no ciphers), busybox's ssl_client and apk-tools (TLS over TCP), and the legacy provider and engines OpenSSL loads on request. None of them imports a QUIC or CMS function or names the AES-GCM-SIV cipher, and the image has no openssl command. Python's ssl module has no QUIC support, and dnspython's DNS over QUIC needs aioquic, which the image does not install. The statement is bound to libssl3 and libcrypto3 3.5.9-r0 and ends when the image moves to an OpenSSL with the fix (3.5.10, or Alpine's patched 3.5.9-r1). CVE-2026-107496 is an endless loop in OpenSSL's CMS_encrypt() and CMS_encrypt_ex(), rated Low by OpenSSL, when they encrypt to an EC certificate whose group order is 1. It is reached only by an application that encrypts a CMS message to a certificate an attacker supplies; OpenSSL's TLS and QUIC code do not use it. In this image the system OpenSSL, Alpine's libssl3 and libcrypto3 3.5.9-r0, is used by Python's _ssl module (TLS over TCP), Python's _hashlib module (digests, HMAC, PBKDF2 and scrypt, no ciphers), busybox's ssl_client and apk-tools (TLS over TCP), and the legacy provider and engines OpenSSL loads on request. None of them imports a QUIC or CMS function or names the AES-GCM-SIV cipher, and the image has no openssl command. Python has no CMS interface. The statement is bound to libssl3 and libcrypto3 3.5.9-r0 and ends when the image moves to an OpenSSL with the fix (3.5.10, or Alpine's patched 3.5.9-r1). Verified for source revision __SOURCE_REVISION__.
